text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A very passive Albanian opposition is doing little to unseat the ruling Democratic party, the editorial says.
- Neritan Ceka, leader of the center-right Democratic Alliance party, said common people would suffer from a clampdown on pyramid scheme companies.
- The government has given in to students' demands for better living and studying conditions.

- Mentor Quku, branch head of the National Front party in Shkoder where they won the post of mayor in alliance with the monarchist Legality, repeated his demand for fresh elections and said President Sali Berisha should resign.
- The Bank of Albania said pyramid scheme companies cannot be turned into banks and none has asked to open a private bank.
- The lek gained ground against the dollar, mark, lira and other western currencies on Monday without interference from state banks.

- Bashkim Driza, president of a pyramid scheme and leader of a small oposition party, said the state was trying to make his foundation bankrupt because banks were not providing enough money for him to pay the returns to his depositors.
- An earthquake measuring 4.3 on the Richter scale hit southern Albania on Sunday causing minor damage to homes but no casualties.
- Two officials from the Albanian justice ministry went to Greece to discuss the extradiction of Albanian prisoners there.

- According to a police source, Voice of America radio said $130 million from pyramid schemes had left Albania on a speedboat from the south-western port-city of Vlore but a chief policeman in Vlore denied that.
- The telephone system needs $180 million more to be fully updated, Kujtim Rama, head of the Albanian Telekom, said.
